Conclusion: All twenty complete cycles and forty encoding cleanups passed the unchanged bounded gate: -9 median handles and +3,555,328 private bytes. Exactly one player was created and disposed, with forty distinct playback IDs and source-clear checks. Final idle handles were 1254, 1254, and 1234. Native HTTP control counters were zero because that control was disabled, not because media requests were absent. The sequential control supports a player-lifetime repair without replacing current HTTP security semantics; it does not certify concurrent cancellation, fallback, stale-callback isolation, or final product acceptance.
